facts.content: Patient reports watery diarrhea for 3 days.
Patient has watery stools approximately hourly without blood.
Patient reports intermittent mid-lower abdominal cramps rated 6–7 out of 10 that precede stooling.
facts.source_text: Intermittent mid-lower abd cramps 6-7/10, precede stool

facts.content: Patient reports nausea.
Patient has occasional vomiting that is triggered by milk.
Patient feels febrile but has not taken their temperature.
Patient reports that fluids seem to pass quickly and that urine frequency has decreased.
Patient states that his brother has had a similar illness for 5 days and is improving.
Patient reports no past medical history.
Patient uses paracetamol as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's father has stage III colon cancer.
facts.source_text: FH: father stage III colon CA

facts.content: Patient lives with his mother and sister.
Patient works in a government office job.
Patient is a social smoker.
Patient drinks beer on weekdays and binges alcohol one to two times per month.
Diagnosed with acute viral gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea and risk of dehydration.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute viral gastroenteritis w/ watery diarrhea, risk dehydration

facts.content: Abdominal pain and nausea are considered secondary to acute viral gastroenteritis.
Family history of colon cancer is flagged for future screening.
facts.source_text: 3. FH colon CA—flag for future screening

facts.content: Recommend oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte and clear fluids progressing to a soft diet as tolerated.
facts.source_text: • Oral rehydration soln (e.g., Dioralyte); clear fluids → soft diet as tolerated

facts.content: Advise paracetamol as needed for pain or fever.
Advise the patient to avoid dairy and alcohol until symptoms resolve.
Instruct patient to monitor hydration by tracking urine output and dizziness.
Provide safety-net advice to seek review if there is no improvement after at least 48 hours, worsening symptoms, persistent vomiting, or signs of dehydration.
facts.source_text: • Safety-net: seek review if ≥48 h no improvement, worsening sx, persistent vomiting, signs dehydration

facts.content: If symptoms persist, consider stool cultures, blood tests, and an in-person examination.
facts.source_text: • If persists: consider stool cultures, bloods, in-person exam
